meta.description: Assigns taxonomy to amplicon ASVs/OTUs (16S, ITS, 18S) with a classifier conditioned on a reference database and primer region - DADA2 assignTaxonomy + addSpecies (RDP naive Bayes), DECIPHER IDTAXA, and QIIME2 q2-feature-classifier (classify-sklearn naive Bayes, classify-consensus-vsearch alignment-consensus).
meta.re_audit_of: F:/OpenScience/audits/_pre-fix-20260919/bio-microbiome-taxonomy-assignment (pre-fix score 86 diagnostic, Reject, Skill Veto T3)

scientific_integrity.detail: All 9 inputs (7 regression + 2 new) used real tools (DADA2 1.34.0, DECIPHER 3.2.0, QIIME2 2024.10.1) against real reference data (SILVA 138 QIIME2 artifacts, both region-matched and full-length real subsamples) and real ASVs (770 sequences denoised from the public moving-pictures dataset). No fabricated DOIs, PMIDs, p-values, or effect sizes anywhere.

practice_boundaries.detail: No diagnostic or prescriptive claims about an individual anywhere; scope remains community/environmental marker-gene taxonomy. Unchanged from the pre-fix audit.

methodological_ground.detail: The newly-found IdTaxa() non-determinism (see skill_veto.determinism) is an engineering/reproducibility gap of the same class as the original assignTaxonomy() finding, not a principled methodological fallacy, and is captured under the Skill Veto instead.

code_usability.detail: All code across all 9 inputs executed without syntax errors and no missing-dependency failures in the reused microbiome-metagenomics-analyst environment. Every finding in this re-audit (including the new IdTaxa defect) was discovered by code that ran to completion and produced a checked, non-trivial result -- never an exit-code-only claim.

functional_suitability.note: Completeness improved: the DECIPHER section now demonstrates training a custom trainingSet from scratch (independently verified end-to-end: real LearnTaxa() + real IdTaxa() on a real 60K-sequence reference, real 770 ASVs). Correctness: assignTaxonomy() non-determinism and DECIPHER flattening are both genuinely fixed and verified. One point held back: this re-audit found a NEW correctness gap of the same class (IdTaxa() itself is non-deterministic; see reliability/agent_specific) that the fix pass did not address.

reliability.note: Fault Tolerance: assignTaxonomy()'s stochasticity is now managed (set.seed guidance, verified effective 7/7 runs). But IdTaxa()'s equally-real stochasticity (up to 4.3% genus-level variance between identical unseeded calls, independently discovered and verified fixable by the same set.seed() mechanism) remains completely unaddressed anywhere in SKILL.md's DECIPHER section -- the same category of gap the original audit docked, now just relocated to the sibling method.

performance_context.note: Memory-budget warnings added under both QIIME2 fit-classifier-naive-bayes and DECIPHER LearnTaxa, matching the original audit's confirmed OOM finding. No new performance issues found.

agent_usability.note: Error Prevention improved for assignTaxonomy (seed guidance, Common Errors row) and for the DECIPHER all-NA flattening failure (fixed code, Common Errors row). Still docked: no guidance anywhere warns an agent that IdTaxa() itself needs seeding -- an agent following SKILL.md's Common Errors table verbatim would seed assignTaxonomy but not IdTaxa, exactly the gap Input 9 of this re-audit demonstrates.

human_usability.note: Forgiveness improved for the two originally-found defects (both now documented and fixed). Still silent on how a user would recognize or recover from IdTaxa()'s own non-determinism, which this re-audit found to be a real, larger-magnitude instance of the same problem.

security.note: Unchanged: no hardcoded credentials, no unsanitized execution of user-provided strings, no sensitive-data handling concerns anywhere in SKILL.md or the two example scripts.

maintainability.note: Testability: the DECIPHER training-from-scratch path is now demonstrated and testable (improvement). But no example anywhere -- old or new -- includes a self-check that a repeated run reproduces its own prior output, which is exactly the class of defect (now found twice: assignTaxonomy pre-fix, IdTaxa still) that ships silently without one.

agent_specific.note: Idempotency: the DADA2 assignTaxonomy() path is now confirmed idempotent under set.seed() (7/7 runs, two different real references, zero exceptions) -- full credit for that half. One point held back because DECIPHER IdTaxa(), a core, equally-documented method in the Skill's own Tool Taxonomy and Decision Tree, is confirmed NOT idempotent as shipped (33/770 and 23/770 genus differences across three independent unseeded runs).

inputs.label: DECIPHER IdTaxa training + classification + flattening (regression -- where the NEW defect was found)
inputs.note: Flattening fix CONFIRMED: old code still gives 0/770 (100% NA, matches pre-fix finding exactly); new positional code recovers 480/770 (62.3%) genus-assigned, closely matching the fix log's claimed 482/770. NEW DEFECT: the small 480-vs-482 gap is explained by, and is itself evidence of, IdTaxa() being non-deterministic even with the trainingSet held fixed -- two back-to-back IdTaxa() calls (no seed, exactly as SKILL.md ships it) differ at 33/770 (4.3%) genus calls, LARGER than the original assignTaxonomy() bug. A third independent unseeded run differs from the first at 23/770 (3.0%) genus, confirming this is not a fluke. set.seed(100) before IdTaxa() fully fixes it (verified multithreaded and single-threaded) -- SKILL.md just never calls it.

key_strengths: The assignTaxonomy() non-determinism fix is completely and robustly verified: 7/7 independent seeded runs (2 different real large SILVA references, multithreaded default config) are bit-identical at every rank including genus, and addSpecies() is confirmed inherently deterministic. This half of the original veto is genuinely closed.

The DECIPHER IdTaxa flattening fix is verified end-to-end from scratch: the old code reproduces the original 100%-NA bug exactly (regression-confirmed), and the new code, copied verbatim from SKILL.md and run via a completely independent LearnTaxa() training pass, recovers a real 480/770 (62.3%) genus-assignment rate closely matching the fix log's own claim.

The redundancy pass on usage-guide.md is real and substantial (50 lines removed, 5 added; verified via diff): it now holds only Overview, Prerequisites, Quick Start, Example Prompts, and Related Skills, with no restated facts from SKILL.md.

Inputs 1, 3, 5, 6, 7 (QIIME2 classify-sklearn/vsearch, Trap-1 comparison, scope/adversarial guidance) show zero regression -- confirmed via SKILL.md diff analysis plus a direct spot-check re-derivation from the original audit's still-live cached real outputs for Inputs 1 and 5, both exact matches.

recommendations.title: DECIPHER IdTaxa() is non-deterministic without set.seed() -- the same Skill Veto T3 defect, now in a sibling method, unaddressed by this fix pass
recommendations.problem: Two back-to-back IdTaxa() calls on the identical trainingSet and identical 770 real ASVs, exactly as SKILL.md's DECIPHER section ships them (no set.seed() anywhere in that section), differ at 33/770 (4.3%) genus calls -- a larger effect than the original, veto-firing assignTaxonomy() bug (1.9-3.4%). A third independent unseeded run confirms this is not a fluke (23/770, 3.0%, vs the first run).
recommendations.root_cause: The fix pass added set.seed() only to assignTaxonomy() calls, following the original audit's P0 finding literally. IdTaxa() is a separate, equally-stochastic classification method (also documented as a core, recommended option in SKILL.md's own Tool Taxonomy and Decision Tree) that the original audit's inputs never specifically tested for repeat-run determinism, so the fixer had no signal that it needed the same treatment.
recommendations.fix: Add set.seed(100) (or any fixed seed) immediately before every IdTaxa() call in SKILL.md's DECIPHER section, exactly as already done for assignTaxonomy() -- both in the existing pre-trained-trainingSet path and the new from-scratch LearnTaxa()+IdTaxa() training example. Verified in this re-audit: with set.seed(100) before each call, two runs are bit-for-bit identical (identical()==TRUE) at every rank, confirmed both with the default multithreaded config (processors=NULL) and single-threaded (processors=1). Also add a Common Errors row and a code comment analogous to the assignTaxonomy() one, and update the Quantitative Thresholds / reproducibility framing to cover IdTaxa() explicitly so an agent following SKILL.md alone gives a complete reproducibility guarantee.

recommendations.title: No self-check anywhere in the Skill catches non-degenerate-output or run-to-run-reproducibility failures
recommendations.problem: Both real defects found across the original audit and this re-audit (assignTaxonomy non-determinism, DECIPHER all-NA flattening, and now IdTaxa non-determinism) shipped silently -- no example script or SKILL.md guidance includes a lightweight check (e.g. 'rerun and diff', or 'assert >0 non-NA calls') that would have caught any of them before a user did.
recommendations.root_cause: Examples are written to demonstrate the happy path only; none include a verification step.
recommendations.fix: Add a short 'sanity-check your output' pattern to both the DADA2 and DECIPHER sections: rerun the classification once and diff, or assert a non-trivial fraction of non-NA genus calls, before trusting the result for downstream analysis.
